messages.subject_clean: At least 1 entry in recordDateTimeCol of recordTable could not be interpreted using recordDateTimeFormat
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bill & Joseph,
the problem here is that there are entries in the record table where species is NA. I didn't know myself this would happen.
The bug will be fixed in the next release (with a proper warning). Thank you for bringing the issue up.

It has nothing to do with the actual date/time format and the indicated rows are also not correct. The NA species really mess things up it seems.

In the meantime, do something like this and it works:

DetHist1 <- detectionHistory(recordTable          = MetaD[!is.na <http://is.na>(MetaD$Species),],

                             camOp                = camop_no_problem,
                             stationCol           = "Station",

                             speciesCol           = "Species",

                             recordDateTimeCol    = "DateTimeOriginal",
                             species              = "Tasmanian Devil",
                             occasionLength       = 1,
                             day1                 = "station",

                             includeEffort        = FALSE,
                             recordDateTimeFormat = "%d/%m/%Y %H:%M")

Of course you can also remove the NA entries from the table before calling detectionHistory.

@Joseph, does this fix your problem too?

All the best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Error: cannot find Exiftool
messages.body_plain:
Dear John and Melissa,
an alternative way to test if R can find exiftool is to run:

system("exiftool")

If R can find exiftool, you should see the exiftool documentation in your console (basically, a lot of text).

Regarding Johns qustion, exiftool is in "C:/Windows/Exiftool/exiftool.exe" ? If so, try

exiftool_dir<-"C:/Windows/Exiftool"
exiftoolPath(exiftoolDir = exiftool_dir)

Argument exiftoolDir is meant to point to the directory containing exiftool.exe, not the file itself.
Alternatively, put the exiftool file in "C:/Windows", i.e. "C:/Windows/exiftool.exe"

Melissa, you could try the same to see if it helps.
Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Detection Maps with sites in different UTM zones
messages.subject_clean: Detection Maps with sites in different UTM zones
messages.body_plain:
Dear Silvia,
this is a rather special case and not implemented in camtrapR. Here's two things you could do:

- convert coordinates to lat/long (or, if you want to create capthist objects for spatial capture-recapture later, some projected coordinate system that covers all points and has meters as linear units, so the distance computation in the secr package which assumes meters works)
- plot two separate maps if the distances are too big - do so by subsetting the points according to the UTM zone

Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Use camtrapR for tables of previously identified images
messages.subject_clean: Use camtrapR for tables of previously identified images
messages.body_plain:
Yes - it is simple.  Have a look at the structure of the stations and the species tables in camtrapR.

Organise your data into the same format - you will likely do this in excel and export as a csv or text file. The camtrapR fields will be needed but any extra fields can come in too.  The dates will be  a hassle.  Don't be too clever and don't use tidy verse and a tibble, stick with base R data frames.

Read the two tables (as data frames) into camtrapR.

The rest of camtrapR functions will all work for organising, reporting, analysing and plotting.

I brought my 350 stations and 400 000 image records into camtrapR this way.  I had used exifPro where you used Wild.ID.  We had to do much cleaning of the data (getting the stations names and the species names, date formats completely consistent) but you probably have that all tidy.

We have considerable R script - if you need it.

messages.subject_clean: Use camtrapR for tables of previously identified images
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
as David said, it is easy to use camtrapR on existing datasets.. The minimum requirements are are two data frames with the following information:

camera trap table:
- station name/id
- setup + retrieval dates
- coordinates (for detectionMaps and creating capthist objects with spatialDetectionHistory)

record table:
- station name/id (matching camera trap table)
- species name
- date + time of records

All other fields are optional. You don't need directory, filename and the deltatime fields for running camtrapR. You don't even need the images once your record table is done. Please note that currently there is no function to filter for temporal independence in an existing record table. The filter is built into the recordTable function.
See data(camtraps) and data(recordTableSample) for examples.
Best regards,
Jürgen
